title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
relevance_reason: Single tiny weight-tied network recursed in depth (nested latent/answer recursion plus deep supervision); defines the TRM baseline for the recursive-reasoning line.
one_sentence: Simplifies HRM into one 2-layer network that recursively updates a latent z (n times) and an answer y, backpropagating through the full last recursion with deep supervision; beats HRM on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard and ARC-AGI with 5-7M parameters.
key_contributions: Replaces HRM's two 4-layer modules, IFT 1-step gradient and Q-learning ACT with a single 2-layer net, backprop through one full recursion (n+1 calls) after T-1 no-grad recursions, and a single-pass BCE halting head.
Reinterprets HRM's z_H as the embedded current answer y and z_L as latent reasoning z; ablations show 2 features beat 1 or n+1.
Ablation table on Sudoku-Extreme isolating full-recursion gradients, layers, EMA, MLP-vs-attention, ACT; reports ARC-AGI-1 44.6% / ARC-AGI-2 7.8% (2 tries, public eval).

setup.loops_train: T=3 recursions of n=6 latent updates + 1 answer update (42 effective layers per supervision step); up to Nsup=16 deep-supervision steps with learned halting in training
setup.loops_test: Nsup=16 supervision steps (HRM protocol: full steps at test); ARC answers by majority vote over 1000 augmentations

claims.evidence_quote: Yet, we can still leverage multiple backpropagation-free recursion processes to improve (z L , z H ). With this approach, we obtain a massive boost in generalization on Sudoku-Extreme (improving TRM from 56.5% to 87.4%; see Table 1).

claims.claim: HRM's fixed-point assumption behind the 1-step gradient is not satisfied in practice; residuals stay well above zero.
claims.evidence_quote: Thus, while the application of the IFT theorem and 1-step gradient approximation to HRM has some basis since the residuals do generally reduce over time, a fixed point is unlikely to be reached when the theorem is actually applied.

title: Universal Reasoning Model
relevance_reason: Universal (looped) Transformer with ACT outer loop and truncated backprop through inner loops on ARC-AGI/Sudoku; includes looped-vs-vanilla FLOP/parameter comparisons.
one_sentence: Ablates Universal-Transformer variants on ARC-AGI, attributes gains to recurrence plus strong nonlinearity, and adds ConvSwiGLU (depthwise short conv in the MLP) and truncated backprop through loops to reach 53.8% pass@1 ARC-AGI-1 and 16.0% ARC-AGI-2.
key_contributions: Looped-vs-vanilla Transformer table on ARC-AGI-1 at matched parameters and matched FLOPs: a 4-layer x 8-loop UT (40.0 pass@1) beats a 32-layer vanilla Transformer (23.75) at 32x FLOPs.
ConvSwiGLU: depthwise conv (kernel 2) after the MLP expansion; only this insertion point helps.
Truncated Backpropagation Through Loops: first 2 of 8 inner loops forward-only; ablations of nonlinearity (SwiGLU->SiLU->ReLU, softmax removal) show monotone degradation.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Models: Perspectives and Misconceptions
relevance_reason: Ablation/critique of HRM's hierarchy, one-step gradient and ACT halting; directly about which recursive-reasoning components matter.
one_sentence: Short MIT working paper re-running HRM: an 8-layer L-module-only model matches the 4+4-layer H/L HRM; HRM's one-step gradient is framed as latent consistency/diffusion training; using the learned ACT halting at inference does not beat running maximum steps.
key_contributions: Ablation removing the H-module (8-layer L-only, L-cycle=1) matches original HRM and trains faster.
Argues HRM's one-step-gradient training is equivalent to (latent) consistency/diffusion training, so its 'biological plausibility' is not unique.
Identifies train/test mismatch: HRM learns ACT halting in training but evaluates at the maximum number of steps; enabling learned halting at inference does not improve accuracy.

As we will demonstrate later, a well-trained HRM on the Sudoku task also significantly reduces its inference steps, down to as few as 2 to 4 steps, which is surprising yet somewhat expected when viewing HRM as a LCM.

limitations: Working paper; results shown as training curves in figures without tables; single task (Sudoku) for halting analysis; no ARC-AGI evaluation; L-only model's outer ACT loop status not separately ablated.
survey_notes: Agrees with TRM (2510.04871) and URM (2512.14693) that HRM's two-module hierarchy is not needed; agrees with ARC Prize analysis. Note the 'plain transformer' here is HRM's L-module with L-cycle=1 inside HRM's training pipeline; the paper does not say the outer deep-supervision/ACT loop was removed, so this is not evidence that recurrence is unnecessary. Its ACT finding (max steps best at inference) is consistent with HRM/TRM evaluating with all Nsup=16 steps. The diffusion/consistency framing is echoed by later denoising-recursion work (2604.18839, 2609.01449).

title: Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator
relevance_reason: Theory and training method for TRM-style recursive latent reasoning; analyzes dead compute in recursive steps and cuts recursion budget.
one_sentence: Formalizes one TRM latent step as a KL-regularized policy-improvement (CFG-like) operator and proposes Deep Improvement Supervision: per-step targets from a monotone discrete corruption schedule, which lets a TRM backbone use 18x fewer forward passes on ARC-AGI.
key_contributions: Policy-improvement view: pre- and post-reasoning logits of a TRM step define an advantage-like log-ratio; a step helps iff the ground-truth token has above-average advantage (Advantage Margin condition).
Deep Improvement Supervision (DIS): each of Nsup=6 supervision steps trained toward a progressively less-corrupted target, integer step index as input, no halting head, T=1, n=2.
ARC-AGI results with TRM's protocol (1000-augmentation vote, pass@2, public eval): DIS-compact 0.8M 24.0% vs re-run TRM-compact 12.0%; DIS-medium 7M 40.0% vs re-run TRM 40.4%.

title: Reasoning with Neural Cellular Automata
relevance_reason: Weight-tied local update rule iterated in time (recurrent depth) on maze/Sudoku/ARC; recursive reasoning without global attention, with depth and parallel-trial test-time scaling.
one_sentence: Neural cellular automata (strictly local 3x3 perception, shared MLP update, asynchronous stochastic firing) trained with BPTT plus sample replay solve mazes, Sudoku-Extreme and ARC-AGI-1, scaling at test time via longer rollouts, larger grids and many parallel stochastic trials.
key_contributions: Shows fully local recurrent cells reach 100% on mazes up to 201x201 (trained on small mazes), 75.6% Sudoku-Extreme (K=1) and 48.8% ARC-AGI-1 pass@2 with per-task TTT and 3264 rollouts.
Training ablation: sample replay, stochastic perturbations and asynchronous updates are critical for OOD generalization; test-time noise improves accuracy.
Niche-Capped Diversity Pruning for parallel trials and per-cell confidence-driven adaptive compute (about 30% fewer cell updates).

title: Equilibrium Reasoners: Learning Attractors Enables Scalable Reasoning
relevance_reason: Controlled study of weight-tied iterative (TRM-style) reasoners vs feedforward at matched layer evaluations, plus training interventions enabling depth extrapolation from 16 to 1,024 iterations.
one_sentence: Frames TRM-style iterative reasoners as learned attractor dynamics; a controlled feedforward-to-iterative construction path and two training interventions (random initial state, per-step noise with damping) let models trained with 16 iterations run 64-1,024 iterations and many restarts, reaching 99.8% on Sudoku-Extreme.
key_contributions: Construction path on Sudoku-Extreme at matched layer evaluations: 42-block feedforward (105.6M) 2.6% vs 2-block weight-tied (5.03M) 32.6%, then segmented online training + 16x depth 74.7%, hierarchy 76.5%, ACT 84.8%.

Randomized state initialization (RI) and noise injection (NI) shape attractor landscapes: Maze-Unique 44.9 to 82.2 at the same compute; fixed-point residual tracks error and serves as a verifier-free selection signal.
Two-axis test-time scaling (depth D, breadth B): Sudoku 86.4 (D=16) to 93.0 (D=64) to 99.8 (D=64, B=128); Mini-ARC 55.28 vs TRM 48.35.

title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning
relevance_reason: Looped Transformer (shared block x8) inside a timestep-free recurrent diffusion denoiser with persistent hidden state; anytime solver whose accuracy rises with recurrent depth far beyond training.
one_sentence: Adds a persistent hidden state to a diffusion denoiser built from a looped Transformer block and removes timestep conditioning; trained with annealed corruption and 4-step truncated BPTT, it keeps solving more puzzles as inference depth grows (99.90% Sudoku-Extreme at K=10,000).
key_contributions: Timestep-free recurrent diffusion: shared block looped J=8 times per denoising step, hidden state carried across steps and never directly supervised; truncated BPTT through L=4 steps on staggered rollouts of K~Unif[20,160].
Inference needs no annealing: constant maximal noise on non-clue cells gives the best Sudoku solve rate (99.90%) and stable convergence, without parallel rollouts or selection heads.
Ablations: annealed-corruption training curriculum is critical (clean-only 0.00%); memoryless models are slower and lower; hidden-state interventions show it carries spatially structured progress.

title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework
relevance_reason: Transfers TRM-style recursion (y/z states, T-1 no-grad recursions, deep supervision, ACT) to language by putting a trainable recursive block on a frozen TinyLlama-1.1B.
one_sentence: Adds a trainable TRM-like recursive Transformer block (residual y/z updates, T-1 gradient-free recursions, deep supervision, BCE halting) on top of frozen TinyLlama-1.1B features and the frozen LM head, trained per GLoRE task with single-token answers.
key_contributions: TRM-to-language transfer: frozen LLM supplies anchor x; recursive block refines answer y and scratchpad z with residual updates and step embeddings; decoded via frozen LM head.
Recall-Then-Learn truncated backprop (gradient-free warm-up recursions then one gradient step) with deep supervision and ACT halting.
Reports 98.6% ProofWriter and 97.6% RuleTaker with per-task supervised training of the block (5,000 training examples each).

title: Recursive Inference Machines for Neural Reasoning

one_sentence: Casts HRM/TRM as Sequential-Monte-Carlo-like inference machines with an identity reweighter and adds learned reweighters (input-dependent EMA gating, RIMA; attention over the latent history, RIMformer), improving over a re-run TRM on ARC-AGI-1 and Sudoku-Extreme; also a Gibbs-style TabPFN variant.

RIMA: learned input-dependent gate mixing candidate and previous state; RIMformer: Transformer reweighter attending over history (lookback max(N,T)).

Provenance error: the paper says 'The 44.9% result reported by the original TRM work is for Maze-Hard', but TRM (2510.04871) reports 85.3% on Maze-Hard; 44.9% is EqR's (2605.21488) TRM number on Maze-Unique. relevance_reason: Transfers TRM (weight-tied 2-block recursion, deep supervision, halting) to combinatorial optimization (TSP, MIS) and scales test-time depth and width.
one_sentence: Adapts TRM to TSP and MIS with graph-aware attention biases, lightweight decoders (2-opt edge insertion, peeling), problem-specific halting checks and noisy parallel rollouts; achieves the lowest learned-solver gaps on TSP-500/1000 and beats KaMIS on ER-[700-800] with 200 rollouts, plus self-relabeling training.
key_contributions: TRM4CO: 7M weight-tied TRM core (constant across problems) with problem embeddings and decoders; depth D and width K scale test-time compute, evaluation may run deeper than training.
Halting on a problem-specific solved check during training instead of a learned head; at test, selection by objective.
Self-relabeling: periodically replacing labels with the model's better solutions; can train MIS from scratch without solver labels.

title: Steering Recurrent Reasoners at Inference Time with Readout Feedback
relevance_reason: Training-free inference-time control of frozen recurrent reasoners (AKOrN, ItrSA++, TRM) by feeding readout probabilities back into the latent dynamics.
one_sentence: Readout Feedback converts a recurrent reasoner's intermediate token probabilities into pairwise coupling forces added to its latent updates; without retraining it improves 4 of 6 model-task pairs (including TRM on Sudoku-Extreme, 68.4% to 74.2%) at comparable FLOPs.
key_contributions: RoFB: closed-loop test-time steering using the model's own readouts, pulling same-class tokens together and pushing others apart in latent space.
Compute-matched comparison with longer rollouts and confidence-based voting: RoFB reaches operating points unattainable by either (e.g. ItrSA++ Maze 83.6% at ~100x less compute than baseline 81.7%).
Sign-flip intervention confirms the direction of feedback drives the gains.

title: One Step Forward and K Steps Back: Better Reasoning with Denoising Recursion Models
relevance_reason: Looped TRM transformer trained to undo diffusion corruption over k recursive steps; controlled TRM vs non-recursive and diffusion baselines on ARC-AGI-2 with matched FLOPs.
one_sentence: Denoising Recursion Models corrupt the target with masking noise and train a TRM to recover it over a k-step recursive window (no deep supervision), outperforming re-run TRM on ARC-AGI-2 at equal parameters (24.9% vs 21.8% pass@2 at 14M with NVARC pretraining) and showing non-recursive and diffusion baselines fail.
key_contributions: DRM: one forward corruption step then k recursive backward steps through a single gradient window; SPRM: noise in TRM latent states during training.
Controlled baselines inside the TRM codebase: stacked Transformer at matched FLOPs (70M) 25.5% vs TRM 45.7% on ARC-Easy; masked diffusion ~0-1%; TRM without deep supervision 34.7%.
Documents that TRM's released evaluation aggregates predictions across fine-tuning checkpoints as well as 1000 augmentations, and that training includes ARC2-Eval demonstration pairs.

title: Generative Recursive Reasoning
relevance_reason: Stochastic (latent-variable) version of HRM/TRM recursive reasoning with depth and width (parallel trajectory) scaling; Sudoku-Extreme, ARC-AGI, multi-solution tasks.
one_sentence: Makes each recursive latent transition of an HRM/TRM-style model stochastic (amortized variational inference with a truncated ELBO), enabling multiple hypotheses and width scaling with a latent process reward model for selection; improves Sudoku-Extreme, ARC-AGI and multi-solution puzzles over deterministic recursive baselines.
key_contributions: GRAM: stochastic transitions conditioned on input and state, trained by a truncated per-supervision-step ELBO (gradients stopped through earlier states), ACT for depth.
Width scaling: N sampled trajectories selected by majority vote or a Latent Process Reward Model value head.
Multi-solution coverage on N-Queens and Graph Coloring where deterministic recursion covers at most 36.1% of solutions; unconditional generation (Sudoku boards, MNIST).

key_contributions: DARC: embedding + looped convolution on a residual stream repeated N = 2*max(H,W) times; DAMP adds a GeGLU channel MLP.
